audit.summary: Jerash posted a genuinely strong quarter — 27% revenue growth, a real 1-point gross margin gain attributed to automation and scale, SG&A leverage, and a $9M swing to positive operating cash flow — with a stronger current ratio and mostly undrawn credit lines. The caveats are structural rather than accounting-driven: VF alone is 57% of sales and the top three buyers are 88%, the 'Others' bucket actually shrank, and the 421% net income jump is exaggerated by an effective tax rate falling from 50.4% to 19.4%. Layer on unsettled Jordan tariff policy (currently exempt only by HTSUS code carve-outs), a fully drawn DBS facility, rising supply-chain-financing costs in other expenses, and hedged language about funding a capex ramp possibly via the capital markets, and the picture is solid execution on a fragile, concentrated base.

green_flags.evidence: Net income of $10.5M for the quarter vs $8.1M, and $29.7M for nine months vs $21.8M; ROA improved to 1.37%/1.31% from 1.12%/1.04% and ROE to 16.02%/15.65% from 14.41%/13.40%.

green_flags.flag: Capital strengthening and deleveraging of subordinated debt
green_flags.evidence: Shareholders' equity rose to $267.6M from $238.8M; equity/assets improved to 8.41% from 7.85% and book value per share to $15.72 from $14.03. The Company redeemed the entire $20.0M of 4.75% fixed-to-floating subordinated notes (floating at 8.99%) with cash on hand on October 1, 2025.

green_flags.flag: Clean and improving credit metrics
green_flags.evidence: Non-accrual loans flat at $3.1M (0.18% of loans), no loans 90+ days past due and accruing, no doubtful or loss classifications, ACL coverage of non-performing loans at 708.69% vs 658.37%. Nine-month net charge-offs of $273,000 vs $305,000. Criticized commercial/CRE loans declined $4.5M to $34.9M.

green_flags.flag: Conservative CRE loan-to-value profile
green_flags.evidence: Weighted average LTV of approximately 57.8% for non-owner occupied CRE, 49.5% owner occupied, 58.0% for multi-family and 58.5% for the office segment; office loans are 'primarily low-rise, non-metropolitan buildings.'

green_flags.flag: Reduced reliance on wholesale/brokered funding
green_flags.evidence: Brokered deposits declined to $31.6M (1.1% of deposits) from $51.6M (2.0%); deposits grew $132.7M to $2.8 billion.

green_flags.flag: New share repurchase authorization signals capital confidence
green_flags.evidence: 'As previously announced on April 15, 2026, the Board of Directors of the Company adopted a stock repurchase program... may repurchase up to 400,000 shares.'

audit.summary: Greene County Bancorp posted a genuinely strong quarter: NIM expanded 41bps year-over-year on falling NOW and CD costs rather than accounting adjustments, net income rose 30%, capital ratios improved, and the company retired $20M of expensive floating-rate sub debt while credit metrics stayed pristine (0.18% non-accruals, minimal charge-offs). The main concerns are structural rather than deteriorating: 66% of loans are CRE with 85% non-owner occupied, funding is 46.5% municipal and highly NOW-weighted with acknowledged seasonality, and uninsured deposit coverage slipped from 128% to 107% as cash fell 24%. Reported profitability also leans on a large tax-exempt municipal securities book, so the widely quoted fully taxable-equivalent NIM of 3.03% overstates the GAAP figure of 2.73%.
